extracted.intended_audience: NASA staff who prepare official correspondence (memos, letters, electronic and classified communications), administrative and mail center personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and formatting rules for preparing NASA official correspondence, including memos, letters, envelopes, electronic messages, faxes, and classified communications; covers header lines, body format, signatures, enclosures, distribution, mailing, and classification/handling rules. Intended to ensure consistent, secure, and record-compliant communications across NASA.

rubrics_metrics.name: THRU: line usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'THRU:' line when one or more addressees are needed to endorse (i.e., approve, concur, coordinate) the document prior to its receipt by the addressee and when the endorsement needs to appear on the original document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type 'THRU:' directly below the last line of the 'TO:' line. The 'THRU:' line addressee signs and dates the memo next to his or her name before forwarding. Single space between each 'THRU:' line addressee.

rubrics_metrics.name: FROM: line format
rubrics_metrics.description: Type 'FROM:' at the left margin, two typing returns below the 'TO:' or 'THRU:' line. The 'FROM:' line includes the mail code and title of the signer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use titles when possible; if an individual does not use a title, a memo may be to a title from a name or name to name. Use full name (example: B/John A. Smith).

rubrics_metrics.name: SUBJECT: line content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Type 'SUBJECT:' at the left margin in all caps, two typing returns below the last line of the 'FROM:' line, followed by a concise statement of the main topic of the memo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subject runs multiple lines, align succeeding lines with first character of subject. Spell out acronyms/abbreviations in subject followed by acronym in parentheses. If frequently used, establish the acronym in the subject so body may use shortened form. Capitalize first letter of key words and do not use articles (a, an, the).

rubrics_metrics.name: REF: (Reference) line usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid a reference line in a business memo except when it contributes to understanding or when number of references is too great for the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type 'REF:' at left margin, blocked, two typing returns below the subject, followed by an itemized listing. Abbreviate items as much as possible and use numeric dates (e.g., 4/5/94). List references as (a), (b), (c), single-spaced in chronological order with most recent first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body of memo formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use single-spaced text with double spacing between paragraphs; type paragraphs in block form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a paragraph is broken into subparagraphs, number and letter them per chapter examples. Hyphenate sparingly to ensure uniform right margin; avoid hyphenating more than two consecutive lines and avoid hyphenating at the end of the first or last full line of a paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widows and orphans
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not begin a paragraph near the end of a page unless there is room for at least two lines on that page; do not continue a paragraph on the following page unless two lines can be carried over.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-paragraph memo spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a memo contains only one paragraph and consists of 10 lines or less, double spacing may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See figure references for layout examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succeeding pages formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Type succeeding pages of a memo on plain bond paper; beginning with the second page, type the page number five lines from the top, approximately 1 inch from the right edge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue the body two lines below the page number and allow same margins as first page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature block format
rubrics_metrics.description: Type the signature information at the left margin, five typing returns below the last line of text. Type the name of the signing official only (do not use Mr., Mrs., Ms., or Dr.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting official and signing protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: If an acting official will sign, type that person's name and the word 'Acting' before the title in the 'FROM:' line. If someone signs on behalf of the signer, the person signing will write 'for' in front of the typed name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark courtesy copies with the actual signer's name to establish who actually signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enclosures labeling and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any material included with a memo is called an enclosure. Type the word 'Enclosure' flush left, two lines below the signature block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify enclosures in the text in as few words as possible or by title. If more than one enclosure, indicate number (e.g., '3 Enclosures'). If enclosures are not identified in text, list each on a separate line. On first page of each enclosure, type 'Enclosure' in the lower right corner (e.g., Enclosure, Enclosure 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Material sent under separate cover
rubrics_metrics.description: When material referred to in the text is sent under separate cover, type 'Separate Cover:' at the left margin, two typing returns below the signer's title or the enclosure notation if present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the material whether or not identified in text. Send a copy of the memo with the material mailed under separate cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy copies (cc:) formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Type the distribution of courtesy copies on the original when recipient needs to know who received copies. Type 'cc:' at the left margin two typing returns below signature, enclosure line, or separate cover listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single space the list, use office or organizational codes, and always use titles on correspondence to outside NASA addressees (titles preferred internally but may be omitted if names listed consistently). Dual-column 'cc:' permitted for long lists. Indicate '(w/o encl.)' after names who were not sent enclosures. Examples and preferred order provided; all lists must be in alphabetical and numerical order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred order for cc lists
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing cc: lists, follow the order: originator's addressees first, Headquarters addressees next, Centers' codes next, federal agencies next, non-federal organizations last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example lists show preferred ordering and notation for '(w/o encl.)'. Organizational acronyms used without spelling out must be well known to recipient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blind courtesy copies (bcc:) and official file copy preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use blind courtesy copies when recipient does not need to know who received copies or to document the office of record. Type 'bcc:' on the official file copy two typing returns below the 'cc:' listing. Never type 'bcc:' on the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the official file copy with the Agency filing scheme number from NPR 1441.1C. Indicate '(w/o enclosure)' where appropriate. Dual-column bcc lists follow same guidelines as cc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of office, writer, and typist on file copies
rubrics_metrics.description: On the bottom of file copies of the signature page, type the mail code of the preparing office, the writer's first initial and surname, the typist's initials, date of typing, and the writer's telephone extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If memo is rewritten or retyped, type a second identification line directly below the first indicating rewritten/retyped and new initials/dates; replace and destroy all previous copies except the official copy and the marked-up copy. Mark through previous official copy with a diagonal red line and staple to the back of the rewritten one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrences: use and documentation (NASA Form 1267)
rubrics_metrics.description: If concurrences are required, use NASA Form 1267 (or 1267A for laser printers) for the first page of the official file copy; concurring officials may have codes and names typed in the concurrence blocks and will sign and date in the space provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As alternative, type mail codes and names of concurring officials on bottom of plain paper (first page) for the official file copy. Signature page will reflect cc:, bcc:, official file, reading file, and identification line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrence signature handling and originals
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes concurring or approving officials must sign on an original document (e.g., personnel, procurement, planning documents); in these cases, format concurrence and approval blocks to show name, date, and title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide signature blocks labeled 'Concurrence:' and 'Approval:' with lines for signature, date, and title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly for signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble memos for signature according to prescribed figures and examples in the handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to handbook figures (4-7, 4-8, etc.) for physical assembly order and placement of attachments, distribution lists, and signature pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-addressee memo addressing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a memo is addressed to more than three individuals, address it to a categorical group; if addressees do not fall under a category, address memo to 'Distribution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study figures for many multiple-addressee formats and variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original vs. photocopy distribution for multi-addressees
rubrics_metrics.description: When addressees are listed in the 'TO:' line, send each individual an original memo with an original signature; if addressees are part of a distribution list, send photocopies and retain the original in the official file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution list formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Type the name of the specific group or 'Distribution:' two typing returns below the signature block or the enclosure/separate-cover listing. Begin the list directly beneath the heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single space the list and arrange in alphabetical/numerical order by Center/Code, except listing signer's Center first. If list won't fit on same page as signature, type a separate page or use dual-column. After memo is signed, staple the list in front of memo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorandum for the Record conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A memo for the record is an informal memo used to establish an official record of telephone conversations, meetings, conferences, or travel. The original is filed by the author for future reference; a 'TO:' line is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'cc:' notation names individuals who are to receive copies. All other memo preparation rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing Slip (NASA Form 26) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NASA Form 26 to direct correspondence or other documents to one or more addressees within NASA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief, informal comments may be made, but do NOT use the routing slip for recording approvals, non-approvals, or concurrences pertaining to attached documentation. Number block to left of addressee's name to agree with the number of action requested. A recipient may add addressees to the slip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorandum of Call (Standard Form 63) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Standard Form 63 to inform office personnel of a telephone call or visitor. Accurately record caller/visitor name, origin, telephone number (including area code), nature of call, and always indicate date and time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Message Recording Pad use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Executive Message Recording Pad to document official telephone conversations when necessary; it retains a carbon copy of pertinent information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be ordered on GSFC Form 20-7A by NSN reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic communications general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep electronic messages short—hold overall length to 25 lines and limit each line to a maximum of 80 characters. Restrict each message to one subject and provide a subject line. Do not use all capital letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Gregg Reference Manual tips referenced. Capitalizing all letters implies shouting.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail usage and security
rubrics_metrics.description: E-mail is an alternative communications tool to facilitate Government business but systems are not secure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never use e-mail to transmit classified information even if encrypted. Sensitive but unclassified information may be sent if encrypted. Follow NPG standards when e-mail is used as the alternative for sending an official NASA memo and for disseminating other NASA information (special notices, press releases).

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail signature blocks and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized signature blocks should reflect official business information, e.g., sender's name, title, organization, telephone and fax numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Management Bulletin 97:01 (Guidance for Determining Retention of E-mail) to properly manage creation and retention of record and non-record messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile (fax) transmission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use facsimile transmissions to transmit official business when there is not enough time to send documents through other mail services; faxes must be followed up by sending the original correspondence for official record purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fax classified information except from secure fax systems located at Center Security Office or some communications centers. Use NASA Form 1120 as lead sheet for transmissions outside NASA, showing sending and receiving Center names, persons addressed, telephone/fax numbers and mail codes. Pages may be 8.5 x 11 to 8.5 x 16.5 inches. Transmissions over 50 pages require Branch Chief or higher signature and full justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telex usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Telex (teleprinter exchange) capability exists but is more costly and slower than fax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use telex only when fax or other means are unavailable or impractical (example: transmitting to former Soviet Union states).

rubrics_metrics.name: NASCOM message network rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The NASA Communications Network (NASCOM) provides operational communications for NASA projects and is an unclassified network; NO CLASSIFIED TRANSMISSIONS ARE AUTHORIZED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASCOM should be used only for mission and non-mission message traffic within its scope; NASCOM traffic uses unique four-character routing indicators. Contact Center message center for formats and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other communications services (priority letter, telegram, cablegram, mailgram)
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers may provide additional electronic/print delivery services: priority letters (delivered within 2 business days domestically), telegrams (hours), cablegrams (overnight overseas), mailgrams (next-day delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Center Mail Manager for availability and use of these services; cablegrams useful when recipient lacks fax/telex.

rubrics_metrics.name: General envelopes and mailing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only Government-approved envelopes and mailers; all official Government mail must be placed in approved mailers and processed by a NASA Mail Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never place official Government mail in USPS deposit boxes or take to USPS Centers. Consult Mail Manager for bulk/mass mailing and permit indicia and for special services costs/restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Envelope types, sizes and prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use NASA-printed envelopes or preprinted NASA mailing labels; use the smallest envelope necessary (letter-sized or flat-sized as specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use any other envelopes without consulting Mail Manager. Do not use window envelopes to mail material that contains national security information, is highly confidential, is being sent registered mail, is international, or is to high-level officials. Do not use staples to secure mailers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address information and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses must include at least five-digit ZIP Code and ZIP+4 when available. Place address within the automatic machine reading zone on letter-sized envelopes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type/stamp/machine-print addresses; avoid script or fancy fonts. Use all uppercase letters and do not use punctuation (except hyphens in mail code and nine-digit ZIP). Use approved two-letter state abbreviations (not in body). For international addresses, place country on last line in all caps. Mail stop/mail code of originating office must be in top left corner and is mandatory. Avoid attention lines; if necessary place on first line. Limit address information to five lines or less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified correspondence: safeguards, equipment, and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafting and reproducing classified correspondence is governed by NPD 1600.2A; use only equipment specifically designated for classified work and store classified material in approved containers when not under direct control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved storage includes safes, vaults, alarmed rooms; only Center Security Offices may approve equipment certification and storage containers. Store related classified notes, drafts, and typewriter ribbons/disks used in drafting the document in the safe. Special stickers exist for disks; obtain from Security Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified correspondence portion marking and overall classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify classification (or lack thereof) of each component (subject, title, paragraph) by portion marking at the beginning of each paragraph (S, C, U). Overall classification of the document is the highest classification of any paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark overall classification clearly at top and bottom of each page. Portion markings: (S) SECRET, (C) CONFIDENTIAL, (U) UNCLASSIFIED. Titles and subject lines are marked at end of sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified document format and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall classification must be stamped in capital letters conspicuously about 1/4 inch from top and bottom of each page. Caveats (additional info) are placed below top classification and above bottom classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common caveats include CNWDI, FGI, FRD, LIMDIS, NATO, NOCONTRACT, NOFORN, RD, SAP, WNINTEL. Refer to NPD/NPR for further instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Classified by' and 'Declassify on' lines and downgrade marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a 'Classified by' line to identify original classification authority when originator's name does not appear on document; include 'Declassify on' line indicating declassification date or event, or state 'Originating Agency's Determination Required' if unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Classified by' placed lower right of front/title page. 'Declassify on' placed lower right of cover or first page below 'Classified by'. For downgrades instead of declassify, use 'DOWNGRADE TO:' and 'ON:' lines with date/event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page, copy, and series numbering for SECRET/TOP SECRET
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply page, copy, and series numbering marks to upper right corner of all SECRET and TOP SECRET documents to assist in page counting and copy accounting; not required for CONFIDENTIAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include 'This Document consists of ____ Pages. Copy No. ____ of _____ copies. Series ________.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of classified correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Classified material may be transmitted only by approved methods; each classification level has specific approved transmission methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential: send by registered or certified mail within U.S. Secret: send by registered mail. Top Secret: NEVER send Top Secret material through any mail system—use authorized electronic means or cleared couriers; log Top Secret material in/out by Top Secret Control Officer. All transfers outside U.S. require Center Security Office approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing and packing classified correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Always address classified material to an activity, not an individual. Double-wrap classified material using two envelopes; outer envelope must conform to NPR instructions; inner envelope must repeat both addresses and include overall classification marked on front/back/top/bottom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach classified material receipt (NASA Form 387) to inner envelope for addressee to sign and return. For internal transport, carry classified documents in sealed opaque envelope; for hand-carry external to Centers, receive briefing and courier card from Center Security Office before approval. If receipt not confirmed within 20 days, initiate tracer action and notify Security Office if unsuccessful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A - Administrator correspondence preparation constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: For correspondence prepared for officials in the Office of the Administrator, write in a clear, direct, and concise style and confine to one page whenever possible; prepare letters in modified semiblock style and memos in block style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval memos should contain the proposed response. Use Office of the Administrator letterhead; suggested fonts include courier, times new roman, or arial (10–12 point). Do not date letters or memos (they are date-stamped by office). Complimentary close/signature block on letters: type five spaces to the right of center. OCIC requires three file copies with specific color/usage rules; keep reproduction and distribution of information copies to a minimum.
